_comment: Shared fixture for the AppMessage payload cap (F-07). Asserted by BOTH
two halves of the guard cannot drift apart again.
expected_bytes is the length in UTF-8 bytes of the COMPACT JSON encoding of
the payload: no space after ':' or ',', non-ASCII characters emitted as
themselves rather than as \uXXXX escapes. That is the quantity the constant
is named after (MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES) and it is the only measurement both
Hand-check for ascii_exact_at_cap: {"a":"xxx..."} is 1 brace + 3 for the
quoted key + 1 colon + 2 quotes + 65528 x's + 1 brace = 65536.
'build' says how to construct the payload:
repeat    -> { key: unit repeated count times }
int_keys  -> { prefix+i: i  for i in 0..count-1 }

cases.name: empty
cases.why: floor case; both sides must agree on the smallest payload

cases.name: ascii_small
cases.why: plain ASCII, comfortably under the cap

cases.name: ascii_exact_at_cap
cases.why: pure ASCII at exactly the cap. Fails on the Python side today purely because json.dumps defaults to separators=(', ', ': '), so the one extra space after the colon makes it 65537. Nothing to do with ensure_ascii.

cases.name: ascii_one_over_cap
cases.why: preservation guard: one byte over must still be refused by both

cases.name: many_short_keys
cases.why: pure ASCII, 4518 keys. The separator inflation is 2 bytes per key, which alone carries this over the cap on the Python side today (65550) while the browser sees 56515.

cases.name: cjk_under_cap
cases.why: the case named in the audit: 11000 CJK characters. Python measured 66009 and refused it; the browser measured 11008 and allowed it. Both must now see 33008 and allow it.

cases.name: cjk_just_over_cap
cases.why: one character further must be refused by both

cases.name: cjk_far_over_cap
cases.why: the direction that matters for security: 30000 CJK characters is 90008 bytes but only 30002 UTF-16 units, so the browser guard waved it through today.

cases.name: emoji_small
cases.why: astral plane: 4 UTF-8 bytes, 2 UTF-16 units, 12 bytes of \uXXXX escapes

cases.name: emoji_far_over_cap
cases.why: 20000 emoji is 80008 bytes but only 40002 UTF-16 units; the browser guard waved it through today

cases.name: lone_surrogate
cases.why: reachable from JSON.parse / json.loads of \ud800. JS well-formed JSON.stringify re-escapes it to 6 ASCII characters; Python must do the same rather than raising UnicodeEncodeError.

cases.name: mixed_scripts
cases.why: ASCII, CJK, emoji and an escape in one payload
